sn21.7:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Vesali in the Great Wood in the Hall with the Peaked Roof.
sn21.7:1.3: Now on that occasion the Venerable Visakha Pañcaliputta was instructing, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening the bhikkhus in the assembly hall with a Dhamma talk, spoken with speech that was polished, clear, articulate, expressing well the meaning, comprehensive, unattached.
sn21.7:2.1: Then, in the evening, the Blessed One emerged from seclusion and approached the assembly hall. He sat down in the appointed seat and
sn21.7:2.3: “Bhikkhus, who has been instructing, exhorting, inspiring, and gladdening the bhikkhus in the assembly hall with a Dhamma talk, spoken with speech that is polished, clear, articulate, expressing well the meaning, comprehensive, unattached?”
sn21.7:2.4: “It was this Venerable Visakha Pañcaliputta, venerable sir.”
sn21.7:3.1: Then the Blessed One addressed the Venerable Visakha Pañcaliputta thus:
sn21.7:3.3: It is good that you thus instruct the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk.”
sn21.7:4.1: This is what the Blessed One said …
sn21.7:5.1: “When the wise man is in the midst of fools
sn21.7:5.2: They do not know him if he does not speak,
sn21.7:5.3: But they know him when he speaks,
sn21.7:6.1: “He should speak and explain the Dhamma,
sn21.7:6.2: He should raise high the seers’ banner.
sn21.7:6.3: Well-spoken words are the seers’ banner:
sn21.7:6.4: For the Dhamma is the banner of seers.”
